title: Proximity Service
oneLine: Index relatively static places by spatial cells, search the user’s cell plus neighbors, then fetch and rank candidates by exact distance and business relevance.
opening: For nearby businesses, the business data changes slowly while user locations are query inputs, so I would pre-index businesses spatially. The simplest production choice is geohash: encode latitude/longitude into hierarchical cells, index business IDs by a chosen precision, query the current cell and enough neighboring cells to cover the requested radius, then calculate exact distance and rank the candidates. Business details remain in a primary relational store and cache. I would choose geohash precision from density and radius, handle cell-boundary cases explicitly, and use a quadtree or S2 cells when density is highly uneven, k-nearest-neighbor queries dominate, or polygon/geofence semantics matter. Reads can be region-local; business updates propagate asynchronously into the spatial index with versioning.
ask: Are indexed objects static businesses or rapidly moving entities?
Radius search, top K nearest, or polygon/geofence queries?
What filters and ranking signals are required?
How fresh must business location/status updates be?
scale: Candidate count depends on density, not only radius; downtown and rural cells need different handling.
Use a cell precision that returns a manageable superset, then exact Haversine/S2 distance filters false positives.
Cache spatial ID lists by cell+filter and business details separately because their invalidation patterns differ.

decisions.default: Geohash for straightforward radius search and operational simplicity.
decisions.why: Hierarchical string prefixes are easy to partition, cache, and query.
decisions.switch: Quadtree for adaptive density/kNN; S2 for high-quality spherical cells and geofencing/polygons.

decisions.default: Choose cell level dynamically from radius and local density; search neighboring cells.
decisions.why: A fixed level either returns too many candidates or misses nearby points at boundaries.
decisions.switch: Precompute several index levels for common radii.

decisions.default: Primary business DB is source of truth; spatial index is derived.
decisions.why: Index rebuild and eventual propagation are then safe.
decisions.switch: Use strongly coordinated update only when a wrong location creates a hard safety/compliance issue.

decisions.default: Filter by hard constraints, then rank distance plus business quality/context.
decisions.why: Pure nearest distance often produces a poor product result.
decisions.switch: Keep deterministic distance-only mode for emergency or debugging fallback.

deepDives.title: Boundary handling
points: Never query only the current geohash cell.
Compute a covering set for the radius and include adjacent cells at edges/corners.
Apply exact distance before returning results because cells are only an approximation.

deepDives.title: Hot geography
points: Split dense cells to finer precision or subpartition by business ID.
Replicate popular city cells and cache common filter combinations.
Do not let one downtown shard dictate the global partition scheme.

deepDives.title: Multi-region
points: Route reads to the nearest region and replicate business/index changes.
Use region/country ownership for data locality.
Return slightly stale business metadata rather than cross-region hop unless the field is critical.

failures.risk: Nearby result missed at cell boundary
failures.response: Cover neighboring cells and run exact-distance filtering.
Adaptive precision, subpartitioning, popular-cell replication, and candidate caps.
Version each business record, invalidate old cells, reconcile derived index, and optionally read-through for critical updates.
Validate ranges, rate-limit, enforce privacy/precision policy, and reject impossible radius/filters.

questions.a: Geohash is operationally simple and works well for known-radius cell lookups. A quadtree adapts to density and is natural for kNN, but tree ownership/rebalancing is more complex. S2 is strong for spherical geometry and geofences.

questions.q: How do you find the nearest 20 if the first cells contain only five?
questions.a: Expand the cell cover/rings incrementally until the current farthest candidate is closer than the minimum possible distance to all unsearched cells, then exact-rank and stop.

questions.q: How do you paginate nearby results?
questions.a: Use a stable cursor containing rank/distance, entity ID, query-cell/version, and filter fingerprint. Offset pagination can duplicate/skip as rankings change.
Highly selective/indexable filters should narrow candidates in the spatial index; dynamic or rich attributes can be applied after ID hydration, with a candidate budget.

mistakes: Using approximate cell distance as final truth
Treating the derived spatial index as the only source of truth
seniorSignal: Choose the spatial representation from query semantics and operational needs, then discuss boundary correctness, density skew, index derivation, and stable pagination.
implementation: PostGIS for moderate scale or geohash/S2 keys in a distributed KV store
Redis cache for cell candidate IDs and business details separately
CDC/Kafka to rebuild derived spatial indexes
Java geometry libraries for Haversine/S2 exact filtering
